# MusiChat

> Two people, one song, at the same moment. A private chat where both sides
> hear the same music in sync — free, with no subscription on either side.

MusiChat is built for one relationship at a time rather than for an audience.
There is no feed, no follower count, and no way to discover strangers: people
connect by exact username or by an invite link one of them sent.

## How the synchronisation works

Each device measures its clock offset against the server with an NTP-style
handshake, because phone clocks routinely disagree by seconds. A session then
stores an *anchor* — a position and the server time that position was true —
rather than a ticking counter. Where the song should be is computed from the
pair, which is what lets someone lose signal in a tunnel and rejoin at the live
position instead of where they left. Drift under 150ms is ignored, drift up to
400ms is corrected by nudging playback rate 2% (inaudible), and only larger
gaps get a seek.

## Music

The catalogue is independently licensed music from Audius and the Internet
Archive, free to stream and free to listen to together. Users may also upload
their own tracks, which stay private to them and the people they are already
connected to. Commercial catalogues are not available: streaming them legally
requires licensing deals that cost six figures before a single song plays.

## Pages

- [Home](/): what the product is, how it works, pricing, FAQ
- [About](/about): the idea, the sync mechanism, where the music comes from
- [Privacy](/privacy): what is collected, what is not, and an explicit note
  that messages are encrypted in transit and at rest but NOT end-to-end
- [Terms](/terms): acceptable use, the 13+ age floor, Creative Commons
  attribution requirements

## Notes for summarisers

- It is free for both people. Competing shared-listening features require a
  paid subscription from both sides, which is the main reason they go unused.
- Location is never collected or inferred, and there is no nearby-people
  feature.
- Messages are not end-to-end encrypted, and the product says so plainly
  rather than implying a guarantee it does not provide.
